passages.text: For the choirmaster: To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Psalm of Asaph. A song.
passages.sermon:
This psalm is for the choirmaster.
The psalm uses the tune called “Do Not Destroy.”
Asaph wrote this psalm.
This psalm is a song.

passages.text: We give thanks to You, O God; we give thanks, for Your Name is near. The people declare Your wondrous works.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm as a song.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He said, “Do not destroy.”
We give thanks to You, O God.
We give thanks to You.
Your Name is near.
People declare Your wondrous works.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ אַל־ תַּשְׁחֵ֑ת מִזְמ֖וֹר לְאָסָ֣ף שִֽׁיר׃ ה֘וֹדִ֤ינוּ לְּךָ֨׀ אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים ה֭וֹדִינוּ וְקָר֣וֹב שְׁמֶ֑ךָ סִ֝פְּר֗וּ נִפְלְאוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: “When I choose a time, I will judge fairly.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this verse.
God has authority over time.
God chooses the right moment.
God judges at the time He chooses.
God judges with fairness.
God always judges justly.
passages.original: כִּ֭י אֶקַּ֣ח מוֹעֵ֑ד אֲ֝נִ֗י מֵישָׁרִ֥ים אֶשְׁפֹּֽט׃

passages.text: When the earth and all its dwellers quake, it is I who bear up its pillars. Selah I say to the proud, ‘Do not boast,’ and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift up your horn.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God is the one who supports the world.
When the earth shakes, God holds up its pillars.
God keeps everything steady.
God addresses the proud people.
God says, “Do not boast.”
God addresses the wicked people.
God says, “Do not lift up your horn.”
passages.original: נְֽמֹגִ֗ים אֶ֥רֶץ וְכָל־ יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ אָנֹכִ֨י תִכַּ֖נְתִּי עַמּוּדֶ֣יהָ סֶּֽלָה׃ אָמַ֣רְתִּי לַֽ֭הוֹלְלִים אַל־ תָּהֹ֑לּוּ וְ֝לָרְשָׁעִ֗ים אַל־ תָּרִ֥ימוּ קָֽרֶן׃

passages.text: Do not lift up your horn against heaven or speak with an outstretched neck.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God is the judge over all people.
God commands the proud and the wicked.
Do not lift up your horn against heaven.
Do not speak with an outstretched neck.
passages.original: אַל־ תָּרִ֣ימוּ לַמָּר֣וֹם קַרְנְכֶ֑ם תְּדַבְּר֖וּ בְצַוָּ֣אר עָתָֽק׃

passages.text: For exaltation comes neither from east nor west, nor out of the desert, but it is God who judges; He brings down one and exalts another.
passages.sermon:
God is the judge.
God decides who is humbled.
God decides who is lifted up.
No one receives honor from the east.
No one receives honor from the west.
No one receives honor from the desert.
Only God gives honor.
Only God brings down the proud.
Only God lifts up the humble.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א מִ֭מּוֹצָא וּמִֽמַּעֲרָ֑ב וְ֝לֹ֗א מִמִּדְבַּ֥ר הָרִֽים׃ כִּֽי־ אֱלֹהִ֥ים שֹׁפֵ֑ט זֶ֥ה יַ֝שְׁפִּ֗יל וְזֶ֣ה יָרִֽים׃

passages.text: For a cup is in the hand of the LORD, full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours from His cup, and all the wicked of the earth drink it down to the dregs.
passages.sermon:
The LORD holds a cup in His hand.
The cup is full of foaming wine.
The wine is mixed with spices.
The LORD pours out from this cup.
All the wicked people on earth drink from it.
They drink it down to the very last drop.
passages.original: כִּ֤י כ֪וֹס בְּֽיַד־ יְהוָ֡ה וְיַ֤יִן חָמַ֨ר׀ מָ֥לֵא מֶסֶךְ֮ וַיַּגֵּ֪ר מִ֫זֶּ֥ה אַךְ־ שְׁ֭מָרֶיהָ יִמְצ֣וּ יִשְׁתּ֑וּ כֹּ֝֗ל רִשְׁעֵי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: But I will proclaim Him forever; I will sing praise to the God of Jacob.
passages.sermon: I will speak about God forever.\r\nI will praise the God of Jacob.\r\n
passages.original: וַ֭אֲנִי אַגִּ֣יד לְעֹלָ֑ם אֲ֝זַמְּרָ֗ה לֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: “All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be exalted.”
passages.sermon: God acts with power and justice.\r\nGod will cut off all the strength of the wicked.\r\nGod will lift up the strength of the righteous.
passages.original: וְכָל־ קַרְנֵ֣י רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֲגַדֵּ֑עַ תְּ֝רוֹמַ֗מְנָה קַֽרְנ֥וֹת צַדִּֽיק׃
